impl.summary:
SPEC section 9 is implemented. Stale and superseded runs are now stopped by question.runtime whether recording is on or off; the recorder is no longer the fence. Six commits on wp/w1-fencing, tree clean, nothing pushed.

API (question/runtime.py):
- RunRevoked (neither ValueError nor TrajectoryError; raising it revokes the run in this process), AuxiliaryTicket and auxiliary_run, run_auxiliary.
- write_verdict (superseded / replaced), start_verdict (strict ownership including the live lease), assert_current_locked (0 SQL, checks only the ticket bound to that session), assert_current (revoked-set check, then one conditional UPDATE; zero rows means one PK SELECT to classify, then revoke and raise; auxiliary tickets need only an unchanged generation), revoke, is_revoked. Small helpers: bound_ticket, assert_not_revoked, write_fence, write_refusal.
- transaction(session_id, user_id, *, fence=True). Runtime callers pass fence=False: start_run, finish_run, cancel_session, recovery, continuation, question.ask/_resolve/save_draft, legacy, set_session_status (which keeps its silent return), suggestions (_current stays the authority).
- still_current and heartbeat use conditional updates.

Insertion points (SPEC 9.2):
- Chat writes under the session lock go through the transaction fence (create_user_message, create_assistant_message, update_message_info, save_part, update_part_data, cron injection).
- update_session adds an EXISTS predicate when a run or auxiliary ticket is bound; token-only writes are not fenced.
- save_internal_part and commit_tool_reveals check after the session lock.
- Loop step top: assert_current("step"). Before the assistant message: revoked-set check. Before the chat request: assert_current("request", progress=True).
- stream_llm and metered_completion check before UsageMeter.start; capture_service_dispatch checks before RequestCapture.start.
- Tool hooks: revoked check before permission, lease check with progress before execution, output and TOOL_COMPLETED suppressed after revocation. Processor dispatch loop checks the revoked set.
- Subagent spawn checks before _run_child; cron flush checks before injecting.
- Title and suggestions tasks run under auxiliary tickets with current_run cleared.

Handling (SPEC 9.3):
- run_loop treats RunRevoked as an abort: no SESSION_ERROR, no error status, finish_run(aborted=True).
- hooks record the tool as cancelled; execute_one returns None.
- Every trajectory-error re-raise site classified F, F+R or R (F nested) in producers.md section 3 now also re-raises RunRevoked (see spec_deviations). Defensive-only handlers were removed.

Execution fixes (SPEC 9.4):
- invalidate_locked clears run_id and lease_until and revokes the run after commit. It records run.interrupted only when run_generation equals generation, so rows that already hold a terminal event don't conflict.
- recover_expired_runs isolates each candidate; a lease left by a superseded turn is released silently (no status change, error or publish).
- tick runs recovery, expiry and resume independently; expire_questions isolates each session; a recording error during apply_answers is retried instead of becoming QUESTION_RESUME_FAILED.
- finish_run(aborted=True) records cancelled/aborted.
- One terminal fact per run and one turn_finish per turn, via an in-process guard claimed after commit.
- Recording-off cron injection now commits both messages, their parts and the callback consumption in one transaction.

All 13 tests from maps/runtime.md are written. Where applicable they run with recording on (db sink) and off, and revocation is simulated in the database only, as if another worker had done it.

impl.spec_deviations:
1. Re-raise sites (SPEC 9.3). At every site classified F, F+R or R (F nested) I added RunRevoked next to the existing TrajectoryError clause instead of replacing it, and left the recording-only (R) handlers unchanged. Only defensive-only handlers were deleted: mcp_tool ×3, desktop_takeover ×2, computer ×2, video_compose ×6, video_production ×13.
   Reason: in wave 1 the default sink is still the fail-closed db recorder. Dropping the TrajectoryError re-raise would turn recording failures into model-visible tool errors or retries, would make bash re-execute or kill a command, and would break suites that must stay green (test_trajectory_auxiliary::test_bash_recording_failure_does_not_kill_or_reexecute, test_trajectory_runtime::test_failed_recording_never_dispatches_provider). These clauses become dead code once wave 2 removes the legacy sink.
   The recording wrappers in agent/trajectory.py (lines 108-114, 484-495, 524-530, 623-629) were not touched, because this package owns only the capture_service_dispatch fence in that file.
2. revoke(run_id, reason) sets only that run's abort signal, through the new session.status.abort_run (run_loop now registers runs with register_run(session_id, run_id)), rather than calling trigger_abort(session). trigger_abort would reach a newer run of the same session, or arm a pending stop that aborts the next run, e.g. the run a regenerate starts.
3. Revocations in invalidate_locked and recovery, and the terminal and turn_finish claims, take effect after the owning transaction commits, so a rolled-back replacement neither stops a run that still owns the row nor suppresses a later terminal fact. invalidate_locked records run.interrupted only when run_generation equals generation, and recovery's silent cleanup records nothing, so production rows that already hold a terminal event don't conflict.
4. update_session writes that touch only token_usage are not fenced at all (my reading of "counters ignore revocation"); every other field uses the EXISTS predicate.
5. "Skip DB when already checked this step" is a ContextVar reuse of the run's own check for 2 seconds (VERIFIED_REUSE_SECONDS), applied only at the "request" boundary.
6. Test edits outside the new files:
   - test_durable_question_failures::test_heartbeat_failure_aborts_execution also patches runtime.get_db_session, because the lease is now extended with one statement rather than through runtime.transaction; the assertion is unchanged.
   - test_durable_questions' PostgreSQL guard accepts any database name starting with openbox_questions, so the instructed openbox_questions_w1 works.
   - test_trajectory_session_runtime's superseded-part test binds the run ticket and expects RunRevoked.
7. Suggestions transactions use fence=False and _current stays the authority; with an auxiliary fence a stale placeholder would stay pending instead of closing as unavailable. question.ask keeps its strict ownership check raising QuestionGone.
8. Test 11: the w1-emitter package is not on this branch, so the test patches trajectory.record with an after-commit fake emitter (available and failing variants). The rollback case lives in test_run_fencing_execution.py instead of extending test_durable_questions.py:196.
9. The atomic cron injection reuses what was previously the recording-on path, now also with recording off: it sets client_message_id cron:{run_id} and publishes MESSAGE_CREATED with parts. The old recording-off path made four separate writes that also published PART_CREATED and MESSAGE_UPDATED.
10. TOOL_COMPLETED is suppressed after revocation, in addition to the output callback.
impl.open_issues:
1. A revoked run can no longer write finish=aborted on its last assistant message or close its own running tool parts. A user Stop invalidates the run before the loop notices, so with recording off the aborted stamp that used to land after a Stop is lost. invalidate_locked does not close those parts either; that is the maps section 4.4 recommendation and open question 4, not SPEC section 9.
2. A zombie run whose lease was recovered by another process still passes the write rule (run_id NULL, same generation). Only recovery in the same process revokes it (open question 2).
3. Superseding a parent does not revoke its subagent children. A child stops through in-process abort forwarding, or through the parent heartbeat (a third of the lease) plus the 10-second grace (open question 3).
4. image_gen and video_analyze call RequestCapture.start directly rather than through the three fenced entry points (stream_llm, metered_completion, capture_service_dispatch). They rely on the tool-start lease check made just before execution.
5. Other bus events from stale runs (text and reasoning deltas, SESSION_ERROR) are not gated by the revoked set.
6. The recorder's own stale-lease check (trajectory/recorder.py:182-187, owned by another package) is still active for the db sink with recording on. The runtime fences run first, except for a cross-process revocation that lands inside the 2-second request reuse window.
7. The terminal and turn_finish guards live in process memory. With the legacy db sink, a second completed run in the same turn after a process restart can still raise IdempotencyConflict on turn_finish; wave 2's keep-first dedupe removes this.
8. Todo storage, snapshots, revert, delete_failed_turn and set_provider_fallback_status remain unfenced, as they are not listed in SPEC 9.2.
9. The new tests (tests/unit/test_run_fencing_*.py) import fixtures from test_durable_questions.py and share helpers through test_run_fencing_api.py; wave 3 may want to move these into a support module.

verify.head: 1749f6ccd96508b0638c2d36557bd98bb38f22e3
verify.fixes:
Four defects fixed on wp/w1-fencing-verified, plus one new regression test. Nothing pushed; every changed file is within the package's ownership.

1. A refused video attach left the job claimed (commit 1e0f79d)
- Where: backend/tool/video_production.py, _attach_completed.
- Bug: the function writes VideoJob.attached_message_id before it saves the file part. When the fence refused that save (RunRevoked, or TrajectoryError with recording on), the handler re-raised and left the claim on the old message.
- Effect: the run that owns the new turn saw the job as already attached and returned True without saving anything, so the finished video never appeared in the chat.
- Fix: release the claim before re-raising.
- Test: test_run_fencing_writes::test_detached_video_finalization_attaches_after_finish_but_not_after_supersession now also checks that the current run attaches the same job (recording on and off). Failed before the fix.

2. A second completed run of a turn after a restart was rolled back (commit 498f740)
- Where: backend/question/runtime.py.
- Bug: the guards that allow one terminal fact per run and one turn_finish per turn live in process memory, and a restart clears them. With the default db sink, a regenerate or plan accept after a deploy repeated turn_finish:{turn_id} with a different payload.
- Effect: IdempotencyConflict rolled back finish_run and the lease stayed. Recovery then flagged a successful run as interrupted (session error, EXECUTION_INTERRUPTED, task_failed notification).
- Fix: new _record_first keeps the fact that was committed first (it ignores IdempotencyConflict), for run.finished/run.interrupted and turn.finished.
- Test: test_two_completed_runs_in_one_turn_finish_cleanly_with_one_turn_finished gains an after-restart variant (regenerate and plan_accept). It raised IdempotencyConflict before the fix.

3. A paid submit refused by the fence left its job stuck (commit b639832)
- Where: backend/tool/video_production.py (segment submit, transcription submit, transcription retry) and backend/tool/video_compose.py (IMS submit).
- Bug: capture_service_dispatch refuses a revoked run before any provider call, but the handlers re-raised RunRevoked with the reserved job still in its pre-submit state.
- Effect: a segment stayed "submitting". It was reported forever as ambiguous_submit_without_provider_task_id and left for operator review by recovery. It also blocked the same request as an in-flight duplicate. A composition stayed "dispatching" and a transcription stayed "transcribing".
- Fix: _close_refused_submit closes the job as cancelled ("not submitted") and marks the reserved asset failed; a refused retry stays failed. It acts only on RunRevoked from the "service" boundary with no provider task id.
- Tests: new backend/tests/unit/test_run_fencing_jobs.py (3 tests). All three failed before the fix.

4. Deleting a session under its run crashed the run (commit 1749f6c)
- Where: backend/question/runtime.py (transaction now locks through a new lock_for_write), backend/session/internal_parts.py (_lock_fenced for save_internal_part and commit_tool_reveals), backend/session/session.py (set_session_status).
- Bug: sessions are soft-deleted, so the "deleted" revocation reason could never be produced. A run's next write hit the owned-session lock before the fence and raised LookupError.
- Effect: run_loop raised LookupError and published session.error "session not found" for a chat that no longer exists.
- Fix: a fenced write by a run or title/suggestions ticket bound to a soft-deleted session raises RunRevoked(reason="deleted"), and the run's own status write ignores a deleted session. The run now ends as an abort.
- Test: test_run_fencing_execution::test_deleting_the_session_under_its_run_ends_the_run_as_an_abort (real loop, recording off). A probe before the fix showed the LookupError and the error event.

5. New regression test, no defect found (commit 37d8338)
- test_stop_then_immediate_send_runs_the_new_turn_untouched_by_the_stopped_run drives the real loop with recording on and off. The stopped run is revoked, the replacement run completes, and no abort signal, pending stop or error status is left behind.

Checked with no defect found:
- title and suggestions after a run ends
- a subagent after its parent is revoked
- cron timeout, flush and injection
- stop, then lease expiry, then send / regenerate / delete / second stop, including poisoned rows
- broad exception handlers on run paths: a swallowed RunRevoked still revokes the run in-process; only the job-state gaps in fix 3 had a lasting effect.

The implementer's spec deviations were reviewed and are acceptable.

verify.remaining_issues:
1. Recording on, session deleted under its run: the legacy recorder raises OwnershipError on the run's late step.finished from run_loop's finally, which also skips finish_run. That code belongs to the recorder and is removed in wave 2. delete_session already clears run_id, so no lease is left behind. The new deleted-session test covers recording off only.

2. Implementer open issues that still hold:
- A revoked run cannot stamp finish=aborted on its last message or close its running tool parts. Production already behaves this way with recording on (maps open question 4).
- A lease-expired zombie run still passes the write rule when recovery ran in another process.
- Superseding a parent does not revoke its subagent children. They stop through in-process abort forwarding, or the parent heartbeat plus the 10-second grace.
- image_gen and video_analyze call RequestCapture.start directly, so only the tool-start check covers them.
- Stale bus events (text deltas, SESSION_ERROR) are not gated.
- The recorder's own stale-lease check is still active with recording on. A cross-process revocation inside the 2-second request reuse window can still start a request.
- Todo storage, snapshots, revert, delete_failed_turn and set_provider_fallback_status are not fenced.
- New tests import helpers from other test modules. test_run_fencing_jobs.py adds imports from test_video_submit_regression and test_video_compose.

3. The keep-first handling of IdempotencyConflict matters only while the db sink is the default. It becomes dead code once wave 2 switches to the spool emitter.

4. Refused submits are closed only when RunRevoked comes from the "service" check in capture_service_dispatch. Refusals elsewhere in those flows still re-raise without touching job state; none of those leave a pre-submit job.

5. Not fencing-related: a message sent within the 0.3-second stop settle window is stored before the synthetic interruption marker.
